artifact.summary: Apple's Q3 FY2026 results show record revenue growth and margin expansion, but the evidence remains incomplete for a conviction thesis: tariff refunds inflate reported margins, management avoids quantifying price elasticity, legal/regulatory risks have expanded, and point-in-time consensus is unavailable. Cash conversion appears recurring, but we lack share count, valuation, and segment-level confirmation. Verdict: No convincing thesis yet.

payload.summary: Apple's Q3 FY2026 results show record revenue growth and margin expansion, but the evidence remains incomplete for a conviction thesis: tariff refunds inflate reported margins, management avoids quantifying price elasticity, legal/regulatory risks have expanded, and point-in-time consensus is unavailable. Cash conversion appears recurring, but we lack share count, valuation, and segment-level confirmation. Verdict: No convincing thesis yet.
payload.leading_thesis: Apple is delivering a strong June quarter with broad-based demand and margin expansion, but the reported margin includes a favorable tariff refund of approximately 2 percentage points; underlying demand durability and pricing power remain unproven until management confirms elasticity and consensus revisions align.
competing_hypotheses: Constructive: iPhone, Mac, and Services strength reflects a durable upgrade cycle and pricing power; tariff refunds are one-time but underlying margins are structurally higher.
Adverse: The quarter benefited from a temporary tariff refund windfall and supply constraints may mask channel fill; forward demand weakens as price increases on iPad/Mac dampen units.
Neutral: Apple remains a share cannibalization and capital-return story; no new product cycle acceleration until AI monetization is proven.
catalysts: Next earnings release with segment-level demand and pricing elasticity commentary.
Quantitative guidance or consensus revisions for iPhone/Mac units and Services growth.
Resolution or escalation of EU DMA, DOJ, and other legal/regulatory proceedings.
Clarity on tariff refunds and whether they are recurring or one-time.
Share count and buyback pace updates confirming per-share accretion.
risks: Legal/regulatory: expanded litigation disclosures on antitrust and EU DMA investigations create tail risk.
Macro/tariffs: margin benefit from tariff refunds may reverse; future tariffs or supply constraints could pressure cost of revenue.
Demand elasticity: management expressed uncertainty about price elasticity on iPad and Mac after price increases.
Concentration: reliance on iPhone for revenue growth; overall smartphone market demand questions from component suppliers.
Valuation: no point-in-time consensus or share count data available to assess whether current price embeds excessive expectations.
payload.variant_perception: Consensus may focus on headline EPS and revenue beats, but the variant view is that the quality of the beat is lower than it appears because ~2 percentage points of gross margin and $0.11 of EPS came from tariff refunds, not operational improvement. A disciplined investor should strip out the refund and question whether underlying margins can sustain above prior trend.

valuation_and_payoff_assumptions.underlying_gross_margin_ex_tariff_refund: Approximately 48% based on reported 50.1% less ~2 percentage points tariff refund impact.
valuation_and_payoff_assumptions.notes: These figures are derived from SEC XBRL and cash-flow bridge computations; no fair value, price target, or probability is assigned. Valuation remains incomplete without share count and market consensus.

unresolved_questions: What is the normalized gross margin excluding tariff refunds and how durable is it?
What is the actual iPhone and Mac unit elasticity after price increases?
Are supply constraints resolved, and was there channel inventory build ahead of tariffs?
What are the latest consensus revenue/EPS revisions and share count?
Will legal/regulatory actions materially alter app store or services economics?

findings.finding: Q3 FY2026 revenue increased 16% year over year to $109.4B, a June quarter record.
Gross margin expanded to 50.1% from 46.5% year over year, including ~2 percentage points from tariff refunds.
Net income rose 27.1% to $29.8B, and operating income rose 26.6% to $35.7B.
TTM operating cash flow to net income conversion was 113.8% vs 109.4% year over year; FCF conversion improved to 106.0% from 96.9%.
Capital returns remain large: TTM dividends ~$15.6B, repurchases ~$82.2B, debt issued only ~$0.2B, debt repaid ~$15.2B, leaving positive cash after returns.

payload.initial_ic_synthesis: Apple delivered a headline beat with record June quarter revenue, margin expansion, and strong cash conversion. However, the reported margin quality is diluted by a tariff refund windfall, management remains evasive on price elasticity, and legal/regulatory disclosures have expanded. Cash generation looks recurring and capital returns are supportive, but without consensus expectations, share count, and segment-level validation, we cannot form a high-conviction thesis. The initial view is neutral-to-constructive but requires stripping out one-time benefits and confirming demand durability before a positive recommendation.

evidence_chain.claim: Apple's Q3 FY2026 revenue grew 16% year over year to $109.4B, a June quarter record.
Gross margin reached 50.1%, up from 46.5% a year ago, but included approximately 2 percentage points from tariff refunds.
TTM operating cash flow to net income conversion improved to 113.8% from 109.4%; FCF conversion improved to 106.0% from 96.9%.
Risk factors and legal proceedings disclosures expanded materially in the latest 10-Q/10-K, increasing tail-risk uncertainty.

claims.claim: Apple's Q3 FY2026 revenue of $109.4B was up 16% year over year.
Gross margin was 50.1%, including a ~2 percentage point favorable tariff refund.
Cash conversion appears recurring; TTM OCF/NI was 113.8% and FCF/NI was 106.0%.

constructive_hypotheses.hypothesis: iPhone, Mac, and Services demand is durable, and underlying margins ex tariff refund remain near record levels.
Strong cash conversion and disciplined capital returns support per-share value despite slower revenue growth.

adverse_hypotheses.hypothesis: The beat was inflated by a one-time tariff refund; underlying margin expansion is overstated and may reverse.
Price increases on iPad/Mac could suppress unit demand, and management's refusal to quantify elasticity signals uncertainty.

hidden_risks.risk: Tariff refunds may reverse or be clawed back, reducing margins and earnings artificially boosted in the current quarter.
Expanded legal/regulatory disclosures could lead to fines, remedies, or app store changes with material impact on Services.

unsupported_claims.claim: EPS was $2.02 and included $0.11 from tariff refunds.
unsupported_claims.note: This appears in management press release text but is not present in the supplied allowed evidence IDs; treat as unverified external opinion until admitted.

unsupported_claims.claim: Supply constraints and sequential FX headwinds adversely affected results.
unsupported_claims.note: Mentioned in earnings transcript but no quantitative evidence supplied to quantify impact.

lessons.lesson: Headline margin beats should be decomposed for non-operating or one-time items before forming a thesis.
Management evasion on price elasticity is a negative signal; require hard volume/price data before underwriting demand durability.

limitations.limitation: Point-in-time consensus is unavailable, so we cannot assess market expectations or revision trends.
No share count or valuation data in supplied evidence, preventing per-share and multiple analysis.
Segment-level revenue and unit detail not fully normalized; demand breadth is inferred from qualitative commentary.
Historical analog dossiers lack retrieved sources and are exploratory only.

monitors.monitor: Next quarterly filing: segment revenue, units, and pricing commentary.
Consensus revisions and analyst estimates once available.
Legal/regulatory filings and outcomes for EU DMA and DOJ antitrust.
Tariff refund disclosures and whether they recur.
Share repurchase activity and share count trend.

payload.final_narrative: Apple posted record June quarter revenue of $109.4B (+16% y/y) with gross margin of 50.1%, but the margin includes a ~2 point tariff refund, making the underlying operating performance less impressive than the headline. Cash conversion remains strong: TTM OCF/NI of 113.8% and FCF/NI of 106.0% indicate high earnings quality. However, legal/regulatory risks have expanded, price elasticity remains unquantified, and point-in-time consensus is missing. Without segment detail and share count, the evidence is insufficient to support a high-conviction thesis. Initial view: neutral-to-constructive, with a need to strip out one-time items and validate demand durability.

artifact.summary: Independent audit: SEC evidence supports the direction of reported operating improvement and permits reconstruction of the rolling cash-conversion arithmetic, but it does not establish that conversion is recurring. Working-capital, cash-tax and capital-expenditure timing remain material alternative explanations. Tariff-refund attribution, normalized margin, durable demand, per-share accretion and the directional view are unsupported by admitted evidence. Several transcript and current-report event labels are classifier false positives. Revision and targeted evidence collection are required.

source_requests.objective: Determine whether operating cash conversion remains recurring after isolating working-capital timing, stock compensation, cash taxes, capital expenditure, financing and capital returns.
desired_confirming_evidence: A reconciled multi-period bridge showing conversion remains strong after temporary working-capital and tax effects are removed and all material investing and financing uses are included.
desired_contradicting_evidence: A bridge showing that improvement is dominated by working-capital reversals, tax timing, deferred payments, temporarily lower capital expenditure or omitted commitments.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop only when current and comparable cash-flow periods and the rolling bridge reconcile to filed statements, sign conventions are explicit, and every input is admitted.
source_requests.title: sec_filing

source_requests.objective: Verify the alleged tariff-refund effect on gross margin and earnings, including accounting classification and recurrence.
desired_confirming_evidence: Direct issuer disclosure reconciled to filed revenue, cost of revenue, gross profit and earnings.
desired_contradicting_evidence: Issuer or filing evidence showing no such benefit, a different amount or classification, or no basis for treating it as nonrecurring.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop when the attribution is supported by admitted primary evidence and reconciled to the financial statements, or remove it.
source_requests.title: issuer_ir

source_requests.objective: Test whether reported growth reflects durable demand and pricing power rather than price mix, supply catch-up or channel timing.
desired_confirming_evidence: Period-aligned product, service and geographic price-volume evidence plus management answers addressing elasticity and channel inventory.
desired_contradicting_evidence: Evidence of weakening units, promotional mix, channel build, supply catch-up or unresolved elasticity.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop when price, volume, mix, supply and channel effects are separately evidenced or the durability claim is withdrawn.
source_requests.title: earnings_transcript

source_requests.objective: Determine whether reported capital expenditure understates economic reinvestment or supplier exposure.
desired_confirming_evidence: Commitment tables showing stable or declining purchase obligations, tooling, prepayments, leases and contract-manufacturing exposure.
desired_contradicting_evidence: Rising noncancellable commitments, supplier financing, prepayments or outsourced capacity obligations that offset lower reported capital expenditure.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop after all material commitment and off-balance-sheet categories reconcile to the latest filing and comparable disclosure.
source_requests.title: sec_filing

desired_confirming_evidence: Official procedural updates identifying active allegations, remedies, deadlines and issuer exposure.
desired_contradicting_evidence: Evidence that changes are drafting or procedural updates without a material change in remedy or expected exposure.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop when each material proceeding is mapped to official status and plausible remedy without inferring impact from text similarity alone.

Apple tariff refund gross margin earnings accounting treatment
Apple purchase obligations manufacturing commitments supplier prepayments tooling leases and off-balance-sheet exposure
Apple diluted weighted-average shares outstanding repurchases and stock compensation

findings.finding: SEC facts support the direction of the primary operating-result claims: revenue, gross profit, operating income and net income improved versus the comparable period.

The primary analyst's rolling cash-conversion arithmetic can be reproduced using annual plus current year-to-date minus prior year-to-date facts. Its evidence array omitted several bridge inputs, so the arithmetic is repairable but the published citation chain is incomplete.
Recurrence is not established. Comparable cash-flow periods show material reversals across receivables, inventory, payables, other assets and other liabilities.
Cash taxes were lower while net income was higher in the current comparable period, so tax timing must be normalized before attributing all conversion improvement to operations.

Capital expenditure was lower in the current comparable period, mechanically supporting post-capex conversion; the catalog does not establish whether the reduction is durable or offset by contractual commitments.

Current-period operating cash flow exceeds the sum of reported capital expenditure, dividends, repurchases and gross debt repayments before other investing and financing items. This supports coverage of those listed uses but not total residual cash or per-share value creation.
findings.formula: operating cash flow minus capital expenditure minus dividends minus repurchases minus long-term debt repayments minus short-term debt repayments

findings.finding: The reported gross-margin level is supported; the stated tariff-refund attribution and related normalized-margin adjustment are absent from the admitted catalog.
Risk-factor and legal-proceeding text changed, but supplied evidence does not quantify expected loss, remedies or Services impact.

Several automated event labels are unsupported by their excerpts: current-report boilerplate was labeled a strategic-priority change, safe-harbor language was labeled a capital-allocation, margin or cost-action change, and analyst questions were labeled management commentary.
Form 4 metadata establishes only that filings occurred; transaction direction, size, price and insider identity are not provided in the admitted excerpts.

constructive_hypotheses.hypothesis: Cash conversion may be structurally stronger if the rolling bridge remains robust after normalizing working capital, cash taxes and capital expenditure across additional periods.
Self-funding may be improving because operating cash flow covered the listed capital uses while reported debt issuance was absent in the current comparable period.

adverse_hypotheses.hypothesis: A material portion of apparent conversion improvement may reflect temporary working-capital, tax and capital-expenditure timing rather than durable earnings quality.
Repurchases may partly offset stock compensation rather than produce material share-count reduction; share-count evidence is missing.
Lower reported capital expenditure may understate economic commitments if supplier purchase obligations, prepayments or contract-manufacturing commitments increased.

missing_contradictions.missing_test: Normalize current and prior periods for working capital, cash taxes, stock compensation and other operating adjustments across additional rolling comparisons.
Admit direct issuer disclosure for the alleged refund and reconcile it to cost of revenue and gross profit; otherwise do not strip it from margin.
Separate price, volume, supply catch-up, channel inventory and product or geographic mix; current management excerpts do not do so.
Reconcile maturities and reclassifications before treating lower issuance or higher current debt as either deterioration or improvement.
Compare substantive allegations, procedural status and remedies rather than text similarity alone, and test whether drafting changes explain the signal.
Compare weighted-average and period-end diluted shares with stock compensation and repurchases before claiming per-share accretion.

hidden_risks.risk: Working-capital sign reversals can make short-period cash-conversion improvement appear recurring when it is timing-driven.
Lower cash taxes can temporarily lift operating cash flow; the catalog does not establish the cause or normalized payment level.
Capital expenditure alone may omit supplier commitments, tooling, prepayments, leases and contract-manufacturing exposure.
Operating cash flow includes stock-compensation addbacks; without share-count evidence, owner economics and buyback accretion remain unresolved.
Legal and regulatory proceedings are documented, but economic exposure and remedy pathways are unquantified.
Classifier errors may contaminate management-quality and catalyst conclusions if boilerplate or analyst questions are treated as management signals.

unsupported_claims.claim: Tariff refunds materially contributed to reported gross margin and earnings.
unsupported_claims.reason: Reported gross margin is admitted, but no allowed evidence ID substantiates the refund amount, accounting treatment or earnings contribution.

unsupported_claims.claim: Underlying gross margin can be obtained by subtracting the asserted refund contribution from reported margin.
unsupported_claims.reason: The adjustment depends on an unadmitted input and lacks reconciliation to filed cost of revenue.

unsupported_claims.claim: Cash conversion remains recurring after working capital, capital expenditure, taxes, financing and capital returns.
unsupported_claims.reason: Rolling arithmetic is reproducible, but persistence and normalization are not; working-capital and cash-tax evidence provide material alternative explanations.

unsupported_claims.claim: Broad-based demand, pricing power and an upgrade cycle are durable.
unsupported_claims.reason: The admitted current transcript excerpt is management commentary, elasticity remains explicitly unresolved, and segment or unit corroboration is absent.

source_requests.objective: Reconcile operating cash flow to net income across current and comparable periods, explicitly isolating working capital, stock compensation, cash taxes, capital expenditure, financing, and capital returns.
desired_confirming_evidence: A filed multi-period bridge showing strong conversion after temporary working-capital and tax effects are removed, with explicit sign conventions and all material uses reconciled.
desired_contradicting_evidence: A filed bridge showing the apparent improvement is dominated by working-capital reversals, lower cash taxes, deferred payments, temporarily lower capital expenditure, or omitted investing and financing uses.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop only when filed current and comparable periods reconcile, sign conventions are explicit, and every bridge input is admitted.
source_requests.title: sec_filing

source_requests.objective: Verify any tariff-refund effect on gross margin and earnings, including amount, accounting classification, and recurrence.
desired_confirming_evidence: Direct issuer disclosure reconciled to filed revenue, cost of revenue, gross profit, and earnings.
desired_contradicting_evidence: Primary evidence showing no such benefit, a different amount or classification, or no basis for treating it as nonrecurring.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop when primary evidence supports and reconciles the attribution or the attribution is removed.
source_requests.title: issuer_ir

source_requests.objective: Separate price, volume, mix, supply catch-up, and channel inventory effects when testing demand durability and pricing power.
desired_confirming_evidence: Period-aligned product, service, and geographic price-volume evidence plus substantive management answers on elasticity and channel inventory.
desired_contradicting_evidence: Evidence of weaker units, promotional mix, channel build, supply catch-up, or unresolved elasticity.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop when price, volume, mix, supply, and channel effects are separately evidenced or the durability hypothesis is withdrawn.
source_requests.title: earnings_transcript

source_requests.objective: Determine whether reported capital expenditure understates economic reinvestment or supplier exposure.
desired_confirming_evidence: Comparable commitment tables showing stable or declining purchase obligations, tooling, prepayments, leases, and contract-manufacturing exposure.
desired_contradicting_evidence: Rising noncancellable commitments, supplier financing, prepayments, tooling, leases, or outsourced-capacity obligations that offset lower reported capital expenditure.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop after all material commitment and off-balance-sheet categories reconcile to current and comparable filings.
source_requests.title: sec_filing

source_requests.objective: Distinguish disclosure-text changes from substantive changes in legal and regulatory exposure.
desired_confirming_evidence: Official procedural records identifying active allegations, remedies, deadlines, and issuer exposure.
desired_contradicting_evidence: Official evidence that the changes are drafting or procedural updates without a material change in remedies or exposure.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop when each material proceeding is mapped to official status and remedy without relying on text similarity alone.
source_requests.title: regulator_court

source_requests.objective: Reconcile repurchases and stock compensation to weighted-average, diluted, and period-end shares.
desired_confirming_evidence: Filed share-count tables showing net diluted-share reduction after employee issuance and stock compensation.
desired_contradicting_evidence: Stable or rising diluted shares despite repurchases, or material issuance that absorbs repurchase activity.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop when share-count movements reconcile to repurchases, issuance, awards, and stock compensation.
source_requests.title: sec_filing

source_requests.objective: Obtain time-aligned revenue and earnings expectations solely to test whether reported operating improvement was already embedded.
desired_confirming_evidence: Timestamped pre-event expectations and subsequent revisions aligned to the reported period.
desired_contradicting_evidence: Expectations showing the reported improvement was already embedded or revisions did not corroborate durability.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop when estimates are point-in-time, period-aligned, and provenance-controlled.
source_requests.title: consensus_manual

source_requests.objective: Verify speaker roles, period metadata, and substantive context for passages labeled as management guidance, cost actions, capital allocation, demand commentary, or strategic change.
desired_confirming_evidence: Speaker-attributed passages containing substantive management statements that match the assigned event labels.
desired_contradicting_evidence: Passages shown to be safe-harbor boilerplate, analyst questions, filing boilerplate, or incorrectly period-mapped.
source_requests.stopping_rule: Stop when each contested label is matched to speaker, period, section, and surrounding context or removed.

Repurchases may reduce diluted shares after employee issuance and stock compensation are fully reconciled.

adverse_hypotheses.hypothesis: Apparent cash-conversion improvement may be substantially timing-driven rather than recurring.
Lower reported capital expenditure may be offset by supplier commitments, tooling, prepayments, leases, or outsourced capacity obligations.
Reported growth may reflect price, mix, supply catch-up, or channel timing rather than durable end demand.

Reported capital expenditure may omit economically similar supplier and contract-manufacturing commitments.
Repurchases may not produce net per-share accretion if stock compensation and issuance absorb them.
Classifier errors may contaminate management-quality, catalyst, and contradiction mappings.

normalized_sources.section: Legal Proceedings
normalized_sources.exact_excerpt: Legal Proceedings Digital Markets Act Investigations On March 25, 2024, the Commission announced that it had opened two formal noncompliance investigations against the Company under the DMA. The Commission’s investigations concern (1) Article 5(4) of the DMA, which relates to how developers may communicate and promote offers to end users for apps distributed through the App Store as well as how developers may conclude contracts with those end users; and (2) Article 6(3) of the DMA, which relates to default settings, uninstallation of apps, and a web browser choice screen on iOS. On June 24, 2024, the Commission announced its preliminary findings in the Article 5(4) investigation alleging that the Company’s App Store rules are in breach of the DMA and announced that it had opened a third formal investigation against the Company regarding whether the Company’s new contractual requirements for third-party app developers and app marketplaces may violate the DMA.

normalized_sources.exact_excerpt: EX-31.1 2 a10-qexhibit31106272026.htm EX-31.1 Document Exhibit 31.1 CERTIFICATION I, Timothy D. Cook, certify that: 1. I have reviewed this quarterly report on Form 10-Q of Apple Inc.; 2. Based on my knowledge, this report does not contain any untrue statement of a material fact or omit to state a material fact necessary to make the statements made, in light of the circumstances under which such statements were made, not misleading with respect to the period covered by this report; 3. Based on my knowledge, the financial statements, and other financial information included in this report, fairly present in all material respects the financial condition, results of operations and cash flows of the Registrant as of, and for, the periods presented in this report; 4. The Registrant’s other certifying officer(s) and I are responsible for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e)) and internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f)) for the Registrant and have: (a) Designed such disclosure controls and procedures, or caused such disclosure controls and procedures to be designed under our supervision, to ensure that material information relating to the Registrant, including its consolidated subsidiaries, is made known to us by others within those entities, particularly during the period in which this report is being prepared; (b) Designed such internal control over financial reporting, or caused such internal control over financial reporting to be designed under our supervision, to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles; (c) Evaluated the effectiveness of the Registrant’s disclosure controls and procedures and presented in this report our conclusions about the effectiveness of the disclosure controls and procedures, as of the end of the period covered by this report based on such evaluation; and (d) Disclosed in this report any change in the Registrant’s internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the Registrant’s most recent fiscal quarter (the Registrant’s fourth fiscal quarter in the case of an annual report) that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, the Registrant’s internal control over financial reporting; and 5. The Registrant’s other certifying officer(s) and I have disclosed, based on our most recent evaluation of internal control over financial reporting, to the Registrant’s auditors and the audit committee of the Registrant’s board of directors (or persons performing the equivalent functions): (a) All significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in the design or operation of internal control over financial reporting which are reasonably likely to adversely affect the Registrant’s ability to record, process, summarize and report financial information; and (b) Any fraud, whether or not material, that involves management or other employees who have a significant role in the Registrant’s internal control over financial reporting. Date: July 31, 2026

Art Levinson, current Chair of the Board, will become Lead Independent Director on the Transition Date. Mr. Ternus, 50, joined Apple in 2001 and assumed his current position in 2021. Mr. Ternus’s previous positions at Apple include Vice President, Hardware Engineering. Apple believes Mr. Ternus will bring to the Board extensive executive leadership experience in the technology industry, including engineering, product design and innovation. There are no family relationships between Mr. Ternus and any director or executive officer of Apple that would be required to be disclosed pursuant to Item 401(d) of Regulation S-K, and there are no transactions between Mr. Ternus and Apple that would be required to be disclosed pursuant to Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K. In connection with his appointment, Apple and Mr. Ternus will enter into Apple's standard indemnification agreement for directors and executive officers . Apple intends to file an amendment to this filing containing the information called for by Item 5.02(c)(3) of Form 8-K within four business days after the information is determined or becomes available.
